bullets.title: JPM raises S&P 500 target to 8,000; Q2 earnings beat rates historically high
bullets.body: JPMorgan raised its 2026 S&P 500 price target to 8,000 (from 7,800), revising 2026 EPS to $365 (+35% y/y) and 2027 to $420 (+15% y/y). Q2 beat rates are exceptional: 87% of S&P 500 beat EPS (vs. 78% 5-yr avg), 76% beat revenue (vs. 70%), with EPS beat magnitude of 29.2% — highest in FactSet history since 2008. SPX YoY EPS growth running +50% with record 16.9% margins.

bullets.title: Tactically bullish tape with FOMO signals; VIX near 13.5, SPX targeting 7,896 near-term
bullets.body: VIX closed at January lows (~13.5), SPX/NDX at new ATHs with upside technical target of 7,896. FOMO indicators elevated: calls-to-puts ratio on SPX at 0.9 (4-year high), short-term call skew at 2-year high. 22V Research notes Risk-On factor basket outperformed Risk-Off by +2.55% over one week with NTM PE spread below long-term median; suggests collar hedges (sell Sept 800 calls, buy Sept 750 puts for ~$2.35) given low put/call skew cost.

bullets.title: Soft July NFP (-23k vs +80k expected) reduces Fed hike odds below 50%; CPI Wednesday key
bullets.body: July payrolls badly missed (-23k establishment survey vs. +80k consensus), driving Fed September hike odds from 57% to 44%. Wage growth declining steeply with employment/population ratio falling in June and July. JPM forecasts Wednesday CPI at +0.12% MoM headline / +0.22% core; 22V flags that monthly core PCE at 0.3%+ warrants inflation hedges. Labor market easing seen as supportive for durable expansion and equity upside.

bullets.title: Hyperscaler AI capex consensus ~$900B in 2026 (+85% y/y); cloud revenue acceleration validates spend
bullets.body: AI capex consensus reached ~$900B in 2026 rising to $1.2T+ by 2027; hyperscalers represent ~87% of AI capex. Cloud revenue strongly validating: AWS +37% y/y, Azure +43%, Google Cloud +82% y/y. Google Cloud backlog +$52B q/q to $514B; AWS backlog $496B (+150% y/y). Hyperscaler FCF turns negative for most of the group through 2027 as capex pressure widens the gap, though MSFT expects FCF positive in FY27.

bullets.title: NDX +5% last week, best since May; Mag7 trading >2 std deviations below mean implying 30-56% upside
bullets.body: NDX gained ~5% last week (SOX +9%), with SPX +3.6% led by Growth (+4%) and Tech (+7.2%). Mag7 +4.3% outperformed. JPM calculates Mag7/hyperscalers' backlogs grew 150% YoY to ~$1.7T vs. capex growth of 80%, and the group trades >2 standard deviations below historical mean, implying ~30% upside to 1-sigma and ~56% to mean. Cyclicals outperformed defensives +4%; Metals +6.6%, Discretionary +4.9%.

bullets.title: Macro regime: durable expansion thesis; cyclicals over defensives, hyperscalers over semis
bullets.body: Multiple sell-side strategists converging on durable expansion view: easing labor market raises implied GDP speed limit above +2% without inflation pressure, allowing Fed to cut on demand shocks. Morgan Stanley favors quality + AI adopters + large-cap Financials over semis; JPM recommends Tech/Cyclicals barbell. 22V notes 50% of past 12 weeks were risk-averse (double historical frequency), suggesting positioning still under-deployed for risk-on.

bullets.title: US-Japan yen intervention (first since 1998) signals macro stress; gold +7%, long yields at 20-year highs
bullets.body: The US and Japan conducted their first coordinated yen intervention since 1998 despite a benign risk backdrop, squeezing crowded short-yen positioning. Long-term Treasury yields posted their largest monthly rise in years to 20+ year closing highs; MOVE index broke its trend. Gold rallied 7% following late-July events, reflecting macro participants' concern about debt overhang. Morgan Stanley expects BoJ to hike in Oct 2026 and Mar 2027 to a 1.5% terminal rate; Fed expected to hold.

bullets.title: TSMC July revenue +45% y/y on AI chip demand; raises 2026 capex guidance to $60-64B
bullets.body: TSMC reported ~45% July revenue increase year-over-year driven by continued AI chip demand, with management forecasting full-year sales growth >40% in USD. The company raised 2026 capex guidance to $60-64B. TSMC and Sony also announced a $6.3B Kumamoto plant for next-gen image sensors. JPM's global memory TAM raised 4-8% for FY26-28E, with HBM pricing expected +42% y/y next year and supply/demand shortage continuing at least two more years.

bullets.title: Memory cycle: HBM sold out through 2027 with ASPs +79% y/y; DRAM undersupplied through 2Q28
bullets.body: UBS raised C2027 HBM blended ASP forecast to +79% y/y (vs. +67% prior); HBM4E pricing likely exceeds $30/GB. DRAM expected undersupplied through at least 2Q28. Samsung achieved ~80% HBM4 yields (up from <60% in February), four months ahead of year-end target. SK Hynix approved W54.3tr ($38B) in investments through 2031. Sequential memory price gains already decelerating — GS/UBS see likely peak in Q2/Q3 2027 before modest declines.

bullets.title: Software bifurcating: infrastructure/AI tooling (NET, PLTR, TEAM) accelerating; pure SaaS under structural discount
bullets.body: Sell-side consensus emerging on a sharp software split: data-infrastructure and developer tooling (NET, PLTR, TEAM, TWLO) bouncing strongly on AI incremental workloads — TEAM +30% and TWLO +25% week-on-week. Pure application vendors (HUBS, INTU, ADBE, CRM) remain under structural discount pending proof that AI expands rather than substitutes demand. Infrastructure Software accelerating fastest in years (DDOG fastest growth in 14 quarters, TWLO back to 20% growth, PLTR accelerating).

bullets.title: INTC launches $15B follow-on equity offering (100% primary); stock -3.6% pre-market
bullets.body: Intel announced a $15B common stock follow-on offering (100% primary, plus 15% greenshoe of $2.25B), with proceeds earmarked for capex and working capital. Pricing expected Monday August 10 post-close. Bookrunners: JPMorgan, Goldman Sachs, Morgan Stanley, Citigroup. The announcement drove INTC -3.6% in pre-market trading.

bullets.title: META +3% on Muse Glimmer launch; Zuckerberg essay advocates open-source AI leadership
bullets.body: Meta released Muse Glimmer, a 30B-parameter open-weight model optimized for on-device inference, compatible with AMD, ARM, DELL, and NVDA. Zuckerberg published an essay positioning Meta as the US open-source AI leader vs. centralized competitors and outlined a vision of free/affordable superintelligence including personal agents and PhD-level tutors. The stock gained ~3% pre-market. Hyperscaler token expenditure costs are down 37.5% from May peak.

bullets.title: AAPL downgraded to Underperform at Jefferies; all-glass iPhone canceled, CXMT chip testing
bullets.body: Jefferies downgraded Apple to Underperform (from Hold), cutting PT to $263 from $286, after supply checks confirmed the all-glass iPhone (targeted $2,060 blended ASP) was canceled due to low yield on glass midframe production. Apple is testing Chinese CXMT memory chips across iPhones and MacBooks to mitigate surging memory costs, seeking White House approval for Chinese-sold devices. iPhone 18 Pro costs expected to surge ~40%, forcing margin sacrifices.

bullets.title: Regulatory pushback on AI data centers building scarcity premium for permitted compute and power
bullets.body: Local resistance to data center growth surged, with New York and Texas joining pushback; Texas facing grid interconnection queues, transmission constraints, and SB 6 legislation. Multiple strategists note that slower regulatory approval processes increase value of grandfathered permits and existing power capacity. Banks are planning a $15B debt offload tied to an Anthropic-leased Texas data center as credit markets assess regulatory risk.

bullets.title: NET announces $2.175B convertible note offering; cloud security seeing strong demand
bullets.body: Cloudflare announced a proposed private offering of $2.175B convertible senior notes due 2031, causing the stock to decline ~2.1% pre-market. Separately, NET reported 2Q revenue of $696M (+36% YoY), beating consensus with SASE gaining meaningful share. Black Hat security survey showed CRWD with largest endpoint market share lead ever recorded and 40% planning to use CRWD as SIEM of choice; security budgets expected to grow >20% by 38% of respondents.

bullets.title: Geopolitical risk elevated: Iran hardening stance, Strait of Hormuz disruption, Pentagon accelerating weapons production
bullets.body: Iran is hardening demands in US negotiations including sanctions lift and military withdrawal while rejecting Trump's Gaza plan. The Strait of Hormuz remains a material disruption — Tenaris cited ~$130M of stuck materials — though Brent retraced from ~$100/bbl toward $80-85 on deal expectations. The Pentagon has asked defense contractors to accelerate weapons production amid Iran war concerns; Ukrainian drones also struck a Russian petrochemical complex.

bullets.title: Hedge fund positioning: continued de-grossing (-1.4% WoW) but hyperscaler exposure shifted from -1.5z to neutral
bullets.body: US hedge funds de-grossed -1.4% WoW (Europe similarly -1.4%) per JPM data, with global equity L/S funds leading at +1.2% MTD. Notably, hyperscaler net exposure reversed from -1.5 standard deviations to neutral (0%), signaling re-engagement with the AI capex trade. JPM advises tactically delaying full deployment until after Wednesday CPI and Thursday Retail Sales prints.

bullets.title: China AI token cost deflation accelerating; multiple models competitive with no single dominant player
bullets.body: Jefferies' Silicon Data LLM Token Expenditure Index hit 2026 lows (1.16-1.18) in early August, down from 2.04 on May 31. Chinese models (DeepSeek, Qwen, Kimi) are highly cost-efficient vs US alternatives — DeepSeek V4-Flash costs $0.03/task. At least half a dozen models are comparably competitive. OpenRouter token consumption grew 21.5% week-over-week to 69 trillion, with DeepSeek V4 Flash ranked #1. Tech companies are setting upper limits on employee token consumption.

bullets.title: TTD double-downgraded: DA Davidson to Neutral ($16 PT), HSBC to Reduce ($10 PT, 28% downside)
bullets.body: The Trade Desk was downgraded by two brokers following weak Q2 results: DA Davidson cut to Neutral from Buy (PT $16 from $29), citing accelerating spend loss and minimal visibility; HSBC cut to Reduce from Hold (PT $10 from $20), implying 28% downside. FactSet consensus target now $14.39 with a range of $9-30.

bullets.title: Morgan Stanley bullish S&P 500 earnings breadth; favors large-cap Financials and quality over semis
bullets.body: Russell 3000 median EPS growth at 15% (strongest since 2021); S&P 500 revenue growth +8% (highest since 2023). 87% of S&P 500 companies beat EPS in Q2 (up from 82% last quarter) with earnings revision breadth rebounding to 23%. Morgan Stanley overweights large-cap Financial Services and within Tech prefers hyperscalers over semis, citing underappreciated AI-related ROI. Stocks with upward revisions to both 2026 EPS and FCF outperformed by 1.6% post-reporting.
